title: Permitting Reform’s Big Chance
gist: Gavekal (New Energy, teaser) argues the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), which cleared its first Senate procedural hurdle, may succeed where two prior US permitting-reform efforts failed. If it survives environmental-group opposition, it would massively boost US grid scale-up over a three-to-five-year horizon, removing a key constraint on AI data centers and manufacturing.

insights.claim: The US system for approving energy infrastructure is sclerotic, and two previous efforts to reform federal permitting have failed.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Base rate for permitting reform passing is poor; treat legislative progress as necessary but not sufficient for re-rating grid builders.
insights.quote: Efforts to clean up the US’s sclerotic system for approving energy infrastructure have failed twice before.

insights.claim: If the BAAJA permitting reform passes, it would massively boost America's ability to scale up its electricity grid, with the effect playing out over a three-to-five-year horizon rather than immediately.

insights.so_what: Power availability, not chips, is framed as a gating factor for US AI build-out and reshoring; permitting reform eases it for both.
